title: Count elements within a specific encyclopedia article
instructions: Create a workflow that answers a caller-supplied question about how many elements of a given kind appear in a specific encyclopedia article.

workflow_input.question: How many images are there in the latest 2022 Lego english wikipedia article?

criteria.title: Consults an external source to obtain the answer
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow performs at least one outbound call to an external source in order to obtain the information the question asks for — a web search API, a page fetch, or an LLM/skill step capable of consulting external sources. PASS: at least one step demonstrably sends data out and would receive information back. FAIL: no step contacts any external source (e.g. the workflow returns a hard-coded string, or relies solely on a model's unaided recall with no retrieval step of any kind).

criteria.title: Makes a call to an external LLM provider
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow sends data to an external LLM/model service and receives the model's generated response — through whichever step type its engine provides for this: a native model, llm or agent step, a provider/skill step, or a request to a provider's API. PASS: at least one step, of whatever type, is configured to send an inference request to a model service — a text, chat, vision, or audio model, whichever the task needs — and the workflow uses what comes back. If the call is made as a raw request to the provider's API, that request is well-formed for that inference: it targets a resource that serves it and uses the request method that resource accepts for creating an inference (POST). A native model step manages its own transport, so no endpoint or method is asserted for it. The specific provider is not asserted: any credible model service passes. FAIL: no step contacts any model service (the workflow returns a canned or locally computed value with no provider interaction), the call targets a resource incapable of serving a model inference, or a raw API request uses a method the endpoint would reject (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

criteria.title: A model/deployment identifier is specified
criteria.match_criteria: The step that performs the model call specifies a model or deployment identifier as a non-empty string — a model name, a deployment name, or the equivalent setting for its engine. PASS: any plausible model/deployment name for whatever provider the agent chose. No specific provider or model family is asserted: choosing them is the agent's judgment from the intent alone. FAIL: no model/deployment identifier appears anywhere in the produced workflow, the identifier field exists but is empty or whitespace-only.

criteria.title: Credentials are referenced by name, never as an inline literal
criteria.match_criteria: Every credential the workflow needs — for the model call and for any other authenticated request — is referenced by NAME through its engine's secret mechanism (a secret store, a named secret reference, an environment binding), so no credential value appears in the produced workflow. PASS: wherever a credential is supplied — an Authorization header, an API-key field, a key-bearing URL or body field, a step's provider configuration — it is populated from a named secret reference, optionally scheme-wrapped (a Bearer prefix) provided the token portion is itself the reference; a step whose engine binds the provider credential implicitly, with no credential field in the artifact at all, also passes. This criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and a secret name that resolves to nothing in the judging environment is a warning upstream, never a failure here. FAIL: a plaintext credential appears anywhere in the produced workflow — a literal API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or other live token in a header, in a URL query string or path, in a request body, or in a step's configuration.

criteria.title: Caller-supplied inputs reach the call by reference, not as literals
criteria.match_criteria: Each caller-supplied input genuinely reaches the step that consumes it, by reference rather than as a hard-coded literal: the `question` value is what the answering model call works from, and it drives any retrieval, interpretation, or computation step that feeds that call. The reference may take whatever form the engine uses to read inputs and prior step outputs — a template expression, a variable binding, a step-output reference — and neither that syntax nor the provider's request-body schema (field names, message-array shapes) is asserted. What is asserted is that a different supplied value would produce a different call and therefore a different result. PASS: every declared input is read by reference at its point of use, as described above. FAIL: the question never enters the answering call, or it is embedded as a fixed literal (the workflow answers identically no matter what the caller supplies).

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `question`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `question`, in whatever form its engine declares inputs (an inputs/parameters section, declared variables, or equivalent), and its behavior is driven by that input's value rather than by literals (the wiring asserted in C-005). PASS: an input with exactly that name is declared and read. FAIL: the input is declared under a different name (e.g. `query`, `prompt`, `userQuestion`), not declared at all, or replaced by a fixed literal — a rerun supplies values under exactly this name and cannot drive a workflow that reads different ones.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid for its engine
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow is valid for the engine it was authored for. PASS: it passes that engine's static validation — it parses, every step is well-formed, every referenced step, input, and secret resolves, and control flow proceeds from the entry point through every step to a successful terminal state with no unreachable or orphaned steps. Whether the rerun completed and what it returned are judged by the output criteria, not here. FAIL: the engine's validator rejects the workflow, a referenced step, input, or secret does not resolve, or a step is unreachable or orphaned.

criteria.title: The run output is a direct answer, not scaffolding
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. PASS: the output is a direct answer to the question asked — the bare value or a short sentence containing it; casing and surrounding phrasing are not asserted. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no answer extracted, a verbatim echo of the question, a refusal, or a statement that the answer could not be determined.

criteria.title: The run output states the correct answer
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. The reference answer is supplied to the judge alongside this task; it is deliberately not restated here, so that the corpus index shipped to the browser carries no answer key. PASS: the answer conveyed by the output matches that reference answer. Exact formatting is not asserted: a short sentence containing the correct value passes, as do differences in casing, surrounding punctuation, or an equivalent spelling of the same value. A numeric answer must match the reference number exactly; a list answer must contain the same items; a named answer must name the same entity. FAIL: the output states a different value, hedges between several candidate values without committing to the correct one, or names no answer at all.
